title: Simplifying: removing pieces instead of adding them

videos.script: Carreto has fourteen deployable services for fifty engineers. {{title}} Nobody planned fourteen. Each one was added for a reason that made sense on the day. A hackathon, a library, a team that wanted its own deploys. {{inventory}} And every one of them still costs something every month. Somebody carries its pager. Somebody upgrades its dependencies. Somebody has to remember how it works. {{costs}} This lesson is about taking pieces away. First, two kinds of complexity. The kind the problem brings, like the rules of the CT-e. And the kind we bring ourselves. {{brooks}} Then Renata goes through the fourteen services one by one, and proposes removing five. Four are gone within two quarters. {{removing}} Last, the difference between simple and easy. Easy means close at hand. Simple means not tangled up with other things. The easy choice is often the one that tangles a system. {{hickey}} And a rule for new technology. Spend it as if the company had only three tokens. {{tokens}} An architect is mostly asked what to add. This lesson is about what to take away.
